geocode.address: BX01 Melrose-Mott Haven-Port Morris (CD 1 Approximation), Bronx

final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**In brief.**
395 flood-related 311 complaints were filed in Community District BX01 (by the record's community board field) in the last 3 years [nyc311_nta]. 6.0% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall in the DEP extreme scenario for 2080 sea-level rise and 2.1% is in its future high tide area, 1.4% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall in the moderate scenario for 2050 and 0.3% is in its future high tide area [dep_extreme_2080_nta][dep_moderate_2050_nta]. 14.1% of this area lies inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent [sandy_nta].

**Hazard Reader.**
The outline on the map is this area's boundary from the NYC Department of City Planning's 2020 Neighborhood Tabulation Areas; a community district is drawn as the union of its tabulation areas, which approximates the district [area_boundary]. 14.1% of this area lies inside the 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation extent (area 5.41 km²) [sandy_nta]. DEP Extreme Stormwater (3.66 in/hr, 2080 SLR): 6.0% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall, 3.4% as nuisance flooding (4 in to under 1 ft) and 2.6% as deep and contiguous flooding (1 ft or more); 2.1% is in the future high tide area (coastal tidal inundation projected for 2080) [dep_extreme_2080_nta]. DEP Moderate Stormwater (2.13 in/hr, 2050 SLR): 1.4% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall, 1.0% as nuisance flooding (4 in to under 1 ft) and 0.4% as deep and contiguous flooding (1 ft or more); 0.3% is in the future high tide area (coastal tidal inundation projected for 2050) [dep_moderate_2050_nta]. DEP Moderate Stormwater (2.13 in/hr, current SLR): 1.2% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall, 0.8% as nuisance flooding (4 in to under 1 ft) and 0.4% as deep and contiguous flooding (1 ft or more) [dep_moderate_current_nta]. Experimental: a satellite model on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2021-09-02, the day after Hurricane Ida, compared with 2021-08-13, showed 200 m² of new surface water in this area (95% of it observed); of 7 other heavy-rain events since 2017 with a clear pass over this place, it showed new water after 3 (2020-04-13, 2023-11-22, 2026-08-03) [prithvi_water_nta]. Limits: a satellite passes every few days and sees 10 to 20 m pixels, so street and basement flooding that drains within hours is invisible to it, and its training labels were the base model's own output for Hurricane Ida, not surveyed flooding; of 153 high-water marks USGS surveyed after Ida, it showed new water within 500 m of 17 (11%), no better than chance (14% of the land it saw lies that close to its new water) [prithvi_water_nta]. Rely on the surveyed and measured record (USGS high-water marks, FloodNet sensors) and NYC DEP's stormwater flood maps [prithvi_water_nta]. Median ground elevation 8.4 m (10th percentile 3.04 m); 26.8% of the area sits less than 1 m above the nearest drainage channel (HAND, height above nearest drainage) [microtopo_nta].

**Live Observer.**
4 FloodNet community sensors inside this area have logged 10 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years, the most recent starting 2026-08-23 10:55 UTC [floodnet]. FloodNet's record showed no flood event under way at them when this was read (2026-10-01 17:36 UTC) [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by the sensors in good working order: 394 mm (15.5 in) on 2026-08-20 [floodnet]. Most events: East 139th Street (7); Rider Avenue (2); Lincoln Avenue (1) [floodnet]. 395 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed in Community District BX01 (by the record's community board field) in the last 3 years: 200 sewer backup, 115 catch basin, 53 street flooding, 27 manhole overflow [nyc311_nta].

**Asset Register.**
NYC Planning's Community District Profile counts 327 buildings, 1,972 residential units and 580 residents in the 1% annual chance floodplain of this district (the floodplain of FEMA's 2015 preliminary and 2007 maps; residents from the 2010 census, by census block) [dcp_floodplain_nta]. 41 MTA subway entrances in this area: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 6 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise), by station: E 149 St (6), Jackson Av (2 5) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 1 flood-exposed NYCHA development in this area (the register lists only developments found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every development): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): MOORE [nycha_development_exposure]. 21 active NYC DOB construction permits inside this area since 2025-04-09: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy extent and 1 inside at least one DEP stormwater scenario (current conditions to 2080 sea-level rise) [dob_permits_nta]. 2 flood-exposed NYC DOE schools in this area (the register lists only schools found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every school): 1 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. Inside the 2012 Sandy extent: Success Academy Charter School - Bronx 1 [doe_school_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): Legacy College Preparatory [doe_school_exposure]. 1 hospital in this area: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure].

**Projector.**
No active NWS flood, coastal or wind alerts for this area (read at its centre), checked 2026-10-01 17:36 UTC [nws_alerts]. NPCC4 (2024) projects sea-level rise in New York City of 14 to 19 in (0.36 to 0.48 m) by the 2050s and 30 to 50 in (0.76 to 1.27 m) by 2100, relative to 1995-2014, as its middle range (25th to 75th percentile); the 90th percentile is 23 in (0.58 m) by the 2050s and 65 in (1.65 m) by 2100 [npcc4_slr].

audit.raw:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**In brief.**
395 flood-related 311 complaints were filed in Community District BX01 (by the record's community board field) in the last 3 years [nyc311_nta]. 6.0% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall in the DEP extreme scenario for 2080 sea-level rise and 2.1% is in its future high tide area, 1.4% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall in the moderate scenario for 2050 and 0.3% is in its future high tide area [dep_extreme_2080_nta][dep_moderate_2050_nta]. 14.1% of this area lies inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent [sandy_nta].

**Hazard Reader.**
The outline on the map is this area's boundary from the NYC Department of City Planning's 2020 Neighborhood Tabulation Areas; a community district is drawn as the union of its tabulation areas, which approximates the district [area_boundary]. 14.1% of this area lies inside the 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation extent (area 5.41 km²) [sandy_nta]. DEP Extreme Stormwater (3.66 in/hr, 2080 SLR): 6.0% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall, 3.4% as nuisance flooding (4 in to under 1 ft) and 2.6% as deep and contiguous flooding (1 ft or more); 2.1% is in the future high tide area (coastal tidal inundation projected for 2080) [dep_extreme_2080_nta]. DEP Moderate Stormwater (2.13 in/hr, 2050 SLR): 1.4% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall, 1.0% as nuisance flooding (4 in to under 1 ft) and 0.4% as deep and contiguous flooding (1 ft or more); 0.3% is in the future high tide area (coastal tidal inundation projected for 2050) [dep_moderate_2050_nta]. DEP Moderate Stormwater (2.13 in/hr, current SLR): 1.2% of this area is modeled to flood from rainfall, 0.8% as nuisance flooding (4 in to under 1 ft) and 0.4% as deep and contiguous flooding (1 ft or more) [dep_moderate_current_nta]. Experimental: a satellite model on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2021-09-02, the day after Hurricane Ida, compared with 2021-08-13, showed 200 m² of new surface water in this area (95% of it observed); of 7 other heavy-rain events since 2017 with a clear pass over this place, it showed new water after 3 (2020-04-13, 2023-11-22, 2026-08-03) [prithvi_water_nta]. Limits: a satellite passes every few days and sees 10 to 20 m pixels, so street and basement flooding that drains within hours is invisible to it, and its training labels were the base model's own output for Hurricane Ida, not surveyed flooding; of 153 high-water marks USGS surveyed after Ida, it showed new water within 500 m of 17 (11%), no better than chance (14% of the land it saw lies that close to its new water) [prithvi_water_nta]. Rely on the surveyed and measured record (USGS high-water marks, FloodNet sensors) and NYC DEP's stormwater flood maps [prithvi_water_nta]. Median ground elevation 8.4 m (10th percentile 3.04 m); 26.8% of the area sits less than 1 m above the nearest drainage channel (HAND, height above nearest drainage) [microtopo_nta].

**Live Observer.**
4 FloodNet community sensors inside this area have logged 10 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years, the most recent starting 2026-08-23 10:55 UTC [floodnet]. FloodNet's record showed no flood event under way at them when this was read (2026-10-01 17:36 UTC) [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by the sensors in good working order: 394 mm (15.5 in) on 2026-08-20 [floodnet]. Most events: East 139th Street (7); Rider Avenue (2); Lincoln Avenue (1) [floodnet]. 395 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed in Community District BX01 (by the record's community board field) in the last 3 years: 200 sewer backup, 115 catch basin, 53 street flooding, 27 manhole overflow [nyc311_nta].

**Asset Register.**
NYC Planning's Community District Profile counts 327 buildings, 1,972 residential units and 580 residents in the 1% annual chance floodplain of this district (the floodplain of FEMA's 2015 preliminary and 2007 maps; residents from the 2010 census, by census block) [dcp_floodplain_nta]. 41 MTA subway entrances in this area: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 6 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise), by station: E 149 St (6), Jackson Av (2 5) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 1 flood-exposed NYCHA development in this area (the register lists only developments found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every development): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): MOORE [nycha_development_exposure]. 21 active NYC DOB construction permits inside this area since 2025-04-09: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy extent and 1 inside at least one DEP stormwater scenario (current conditions to 2080 sea-level rise) [dob_permits_nta]. 2 flood-exposed NYC DOE schools in this area (the register lists only schools found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every school): 1 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. Inside the 2012 Sandy extent: Success Academy Charter School - Bronx 1 [doe_school_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): Legacy College Preparatory [doe_school_exposure]. 1 hospital in this area: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure].
